leads.summary: The CLI treats nonempty but invalid shell.json as a valid mutation seed while the shell preserves its last good parse
leads.consequence: After the shell has loaded a user's plugin/layout settings, a short, syntactically valid partial write such as {} is rejected by the shell (missing version), but omarchy bar position bottom accepts it, NORMALIZE creates version 1 and empty plugin/layout arrays, and the commit permanently overwrites the user's configuration. The new zero-byte check does not cover this validator mismatch. The same mismatch applies to nonempty null, [] or an old-version object.
leads.triage: verified by coordinator source read; pre-existing, unchanged from base; not published (torn writes yield invalid JSON rejected by jq -e, not {} )

leads.summary: Two open competing shell.json-preservation PRs overlap the precise applyShellConfig branch and cannot be merged without reconciling behavior
leads.location: shell/shell.qml:55-108; open PR #12992 shell/shell.qml:58-105; open PR #7723 shell/shell.qml:72-95
leads.consequence: If #7723's branch replaces this PR's logic, an empty (not malformed) file resets to defaults, defeating the fix. If #12992's branch replaces it, a missing file after a valid load never resets to defaults, and a shell-side mutation before any valid file load does not set its hasAppliedUserShellConfig flag. Either replacement also fails this PR's source-pattern tests in plugins-test.sh:217-231. A merged implementation must retain the distinction between missing and invalid/empty plus the persist refresh, rather than taking either overlapping hunk wholesale.
leads.triage: verified by coordinator (gh api PRs, source reads); published as note, attribution corrected via fact check D1

leads.summary: The new 0-byte regression test passes on an unrelated commit failure
leads.consequence: The test captures only a nonzero exit and unchanged file and suppresses the command's stderr. If jq is absent/fails, mktemp fails, or another error prevents commit, both assertions still pass, even when the empty-file guard is removed and source_file would choose the shipped defaults. Thus its TAP success does not by itself demonstrate that the new guard rejected the empty input.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (T1 nit); published in optional test note

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up on the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13104#issuecomment-5825486578) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13104#issuecomment-5825678289), checked at `9805237`.

**Verified:** the three findings from the earlier review are resolved, the load-error one for permission errors (other error types were not exercised). No regression was found in the changed code or in the callers of `source_file`/`commit`. The earlier note about restarts with a 0-byte file still applies unchanged.

| Earlier item | At `9805237` | How it was checked |
|---|---|---|
| `lastUserConfig` not refreshed by shell writes | **Resolved** | Headless Quickshell 0.3.1 harness, 3 runs per revision |
| `commit`-based `omarchy bar` commands reset a 0-byte file | **Resolved** (commands now refuse) | All 5 subcommands, head vs base |
| Every load failure treated as missing | **Resolved** for permission errors | Harness (`chmod 000`, delete) plus Quickshell source |
| Restart with a 0-byte file starts from defaults (note) | Still present, unchanged | Harness |
| New checks are source regexes (test note) | Partly addressed | Test runs with negative controls |

### Resolved findings

**Shell writes now update `lastUserConfig`.** `persistShellConfig` sets `lastUserConfig = payload`, and every shell-side writer goes through it. In the harness (5 shell writes, truncate to 0 bytes, 1 more write):

| Revision | Final `shell.json` |
|---|---|
| base `28ceaae` | defaults + last change, `plugins: []` |
| earlier head `278af04` | user config + last change; the 5 earlier writes lost |
| `9805237` | all 5 writes, the last change and the third-party plugin kept (3 of 3 runs) |

**`commit` refuses a 0-byte file.** On a 0-byte `shell.json`, `use`, `reset`, `defaults`, `position` and `transparent` now exit 1 with `shell.json is empty; refusing to overwrite it with defaults`. The file stays at 0 bytes, `reloadConfig` is not called and no temp file is left behind. Missing, valid, whitespace-only and invalid-JSON files behave as on base. The new test passes on head and fails when base's `bin/omarchy-shell-config` is swapped in. The existing `omarchy-bar` checks in `config-test.sh` pass 19 of 19 on head and base.

**Optional:** in that state the menu's position and transparency actions now fail, and the error does not say how to recover. Naming a way out (for example any change through the shell, or `omarchy refresh shell`) would help.

**Only `FileNotFound` counts as missing.** At runtime `error` arrives as a number and `FileViewError.FileNotFound === 2` compares correctly. After `chmod 000`, head keeps the config (base and `278af04` switched to defaults); deleting the file still resets to defaults. `Unknown` errors were not exercised.

### Unchanged

**Note:** the retained config still lives only in memory. With a 0-byte file at startup, head uses defaults and the next shell-side write saves defaults plus the change, as on base. The CLI now refuses to write defaults over a 0-byte file, but the shell still does so after a restart. Writing the retained config back when the running shell sees the file become empty (not for invalid JSON) would cover truncations while the shell is up; a file that is already empty at startup has nothing retained to restore.

**Optional test improvement:** the commit path now has a behavioral test. The `persistShellConfig` and `onLoadFailed` checks are still source regexes (they fail against `278af04`'s `shell.qml` but do not exercise the rollback). The commit test also passes on any non-zero exit that leaves the file untouched, since stderr is discarded; asserting the `refusing to overwrite` message would tie it to the new guard.

### Related, outside this diff

**Non-atomic `mv` in `commit` (hypothesis for part of #12990).** `commit` creates its temp file with a bare `mktemp` (in `$TMPDIR`, normally `/tmp`) and then `mv`s it over `shell.json`. When `/tmp` is on another filesystem, GNU `mv` removes the destination and then copies, so `shell.json` is briefly missing and then partly written.

```text
omarchy bar position ...  ->  mv across filesystems
  shell.json removed  ->  (if the watcher reads in this gap) FileNotFound  ->  lastUserConfig cleared, defaults shown
  shell.json copied   ->  watcher: loaded        ->  config restored
```

In a sandbox with HOME and TMPDIR on separate tmpfs mounts, 60 `omarchy-bar position` calls produced 7 transient `FileNotFound` events in 1 of 3 runs, each showing defaults (`plugins: []`) for under 10 ms (0 to 8 ms), with this PR's shell code. Same-filesystem runs showed none. This has not been shown to cause the reporter's lasting 0-byte file.

**Impact:** a shell-side write landing in that window would persist defaults, the same reset this PR guards against.

**Suggested change:** `_SHELL_CONFIG_TMP=$(mktemp "$CONFIG_FILE.XXXXXX")`, so `mv` is a same-filesystem rename. Four migrations that edit `shell.json` use the same `mktemp` + `mv` pattern.

**Overlapping open PRs:** #12992 (which also fixes #12990) and the older #7723 (keeps the last good config on parse failures) change the same `applyShellConfig` branch in `shell/shell.qml`. They behave differently: #7723 forgets the retained config when the file reads as empty, and #12992 keeps it even after the file is deleted. They are alternatives to this PR rather than additions.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Pinned head `9805237`, earlier reviewed head `278af04`, base `28ceaae`. Source review of the changed files, their callers, Quickshell v0.3.1 `FileView` and coreutils 9.11 `mv`. Runtime checks used `test/shell.d/plugins-test.sh`, the `omarchy-bar` section of `config-test.sh`, a sandboxed `omarchy-bar` commit matrix with a stubbed `omarchy-shell`, and an offscreen Quickshell 0.3.1 harness that loads each revision's config-handling blocks verbatim (no plugin registry, bar or widgets). The full shell, a desktop session and `omarchy update` were not run. The overlapping PRs were compared by source only.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
